welcome.zh:
欢迎！PHL103H5 是哲学导论，副标题是“知识与实在”（Knowledge and Reality）。在这门课里，哲学（**philosophy**）就是认真追问几类大问题：哲学本身是什么、有什么用？什么东西真实存在（形而上学，**metaphysics**）？我们凭什么说自己知道（认识论，**epistemology**）？心灵和意识又是什么？本站现在收录八周：第 2–5 周是测验 1 的范围（10 月 14 日已经考完），期末还会再考；第 7–10 周是测验 2 的范围。
第 2 周：哲学从哪里开始？竟然有东西存在，为什么值得惊奇？哲学很少给出确定的答案，它的价值又在哪里？（哈特 **Hart**、罗素 **Russell**）
第 3 周：苏格拉底为什么宁可死，也不肯停止审视别人？虔敬到底是什么？（柏拉图 **Plato** 的《申辩篇》Apology 和《游叙弗伦篇》Euthyphro）
第 4 周：美德能教吗？知识和真意见有什么不同？（柏拉图的《美诺篇》Meno）
第 5 周：有没有什么东西，是连最强的怀疑也动摇不了的？（笛卡尔 **Descartes** 的第一、第二沉思）
第 7 周：桌子真的是我们看到的样子吗？有没有不取决于人心的客观真理？（罗素 **Russell**、范·因瓦根 **van Inwagen**）
第 8 周：我们凭什么相信太阳明天还会升起？同样的证据，为什么我们认为它只确证“绿”，不确证“grue”？（休谟 **Hume**、古德曼 **Goodman**）
第 9 周：成为一只蝙蝠是什么样子？把大脑一点点换成电脑元件，你还会有意识吗？（内格尔 **Nagel**、查默斯 **Chalmers**）
第 10 周：和聊天机器人说话时，我们到底在和谁说话？（查默斯 **Chalmers**）
不用怕：这门课没有先修要求，也不用数学。哲学不是背名言，而是看懂论证（**argument**）：作者从哪些前提（**premise**）推出什么结论（**conclusion**），每个例子想说明什么，别人会怎么反驳，作者又怎么回应。真正的难点是英文：读物是英文的，测验也全用英文作答。所以本站先用大白话中文把每篇读物讲懂，再给你能直接写上考卷的英文句子。测验 2 在 11 月 23 日周一下午 1 点那节课上考，50 分钟，题型可能有选择题、简答题和小论文（**short essay**），大纲没有说各有几道。期末考试 3 小时，考全学期内容，在 12 月的考试周，日期由教务处（Registrar）安排。一篇读物、一个论证地来，你能学会。
welcome.en:
Welcome! PHL103H5 is Introduction to Philosophy: Knowledge and Reality. In this course, **philosophy** means asking a few kinds of big questions carefully: what is philosophy itself, and what is it for? What is really there (**metaphysics**)? How can we know anything (**epistemology**)? What are the mind and consciousness? The station now covers eight weeks: Weeks 2-5 were on Test 1 (written on Oct 14) and come back on the final exam, and Weeks 7-10 are on Test 2.
Week 2: where does philosophy begin, why is it a wonder that anything exists at all, and what is philosophy worth if it rarely gives definite answers? (Hart, Russell)
Week 3: why would Socrates rather die than stop examining people, and what is piety? (Plato's Apology and Euthyphro)
Week 4: can virtue be taught, and how does knowledge differ from true opinion? (Plato's Meno)
Week 5: is there anything that even the strongest doubt cannot shake? (Descartes' First and Second Meditations)
Week 7: is the table really the way it looks, and is there objective truth that does not depend on our minds? (Russell, van Inwagen)
Week 8: why do we believe the sun will rise tomorrow, and why do we think the same evidence confirms 'green' but not 'grue'? (Hume, Goodman)
Week 9: what is it like to be a bat, and would you still be conscious if your brain were replaced, bit by bit, by computer parts? (Nagel, Chalmers)
Week 10: when we talk to a chatbot, who or what are we talking to? (Chalmers)
Do not be afraid: the course has no prerequisites and no maths. Philosophy here is not about memorizing famous sayings; it is about understanding **arguments**: which **premises** lead an author to which **conclusion**, what each example is meant to show, how someone could object, and how the author replies. The real challenge is English: the readings are in English and every test is answered in English. So this site first explains each reading in plain Chinese and then gives you English sentences you can write on the test. Test 2 is in the Monday 1 PM class on Nov 23: 50 minutes, with some or all of multiple-choice, short-answer and **short-essay** questions; the syllabus does not say how many of each. The 3-hour final exam covers the whole course and falls in the December exam period; the Registrar sets the date. Go one reading and one argument at a time. You can do this.

howToUse.zh: 先看下面的「知识地图」。八周分成四条主线：第 2、3 周讲哲学本身（**philosophy**：哲学是什么，惊奇，哲学的价值，苏格拉底的追问），第 7 周讲实在（**reality**：表象背后有什么，有没有客观真理），第 4、5、8 周讲知识（**knowledge**：知识和真意见有什么不同，什么经得起怀疑，凭什么从看到的推到没看到的），第 9、10 周讲心灵（**mind**：意识是什么，机器和 AI 有没有心灵）。下面还有一条贯穿八周的线（怎样读论证、评论证），以及“课与课怎么连起来”。八周之间处处呼应，期末又考全学期，所以别把每周孤立地背。
howToUse.en: Start with The big picture below. The eight weeks form four branches: Weeks 2 and 3 are about **philosophy** itself (what it is, wonder, its value and Socrates' questioning), Week 7 about **reality** (what lies behind appearances, and whether there is objective truth), Weeks 4, 5 and 8 about **knowledge** (how knowledge differs from true opinion, what survives doubt, and how we get from what we have observed to what we have not), and Weeks 9 and 10 about the **mind** (what consciousness is, and whether machines and AI have minds). Under them runs one thread through all eight weeks (how to read and assess an argument), followed by How the lessons connect. The weeks answer each other at every turn and the final exam covers the whole term, so do not learn each week in isolation.

howToUse.zh: 为什么一直讲论证？大纲写的学习目标是：读懂哲学原著，从文章里提取并概括论证，解释并评价核心观点和论证，再用清楚的文字写出来。所以每篇读物都按同一个方式讲：作者要回答什么问题，他的论点（**thesis**）是什么，论证的标准形式（**standard form**：P1、P2……最后是 C），每个前提为什么可信、用哪个例子支持，再看反驳和回应。两个词要分清：有效（**valid**）是“如果前提都真，结论就一定真”；可靠（**sound**）是“有效，而且前提真的都真”。评一个论证，就问两件事：前提真吗？推得出结论吗？
howToUse.en: Why so much about arguments? The syllabus outcomes are understanding primary philosophical texts, extracting and summarizing arguments from them, explaining and offering critical perspective on core ideas and arguments, and writing about them clearly. So every reading is taught the same way: the question the author answers, the **thesis**, the argument in **standard form** (P1, P2, ... and then C), why each premise is believable and which example supports it, and then the objections and replies. Keep two words apart: an argument is **valid** if its conclusion must be true whenever its premises are true, and **sound** if it is valid and its premises really are true. To assess an argument, ask two things: are the premises true, and does the conclusion follow?

howToUse.zh: 在「学习 Learn」里按周读。第 2 周 13 节，其他每周 14 节；每节只讲一篇读物，标题以作者开头（比如“罗素：……”），柏拉图的对话则以篇名开头（比如“申辩篇：……”“美诺篇：……”），并标着「读物 Reading」页码，也就是 Quercus 上那份 PDF 的页码，方便你对照原文；柏拉图的对话还会给出页边印的段落编号（比如 21d）。第 2、3、4、5、7、8、9 周的最后一节是对比，标题以“比较：”开头，没有单独的页码：第 2、3、7、8、9 周比较这一周的两篇读物，第 4 周比较《美诺篇》的前后两半，第 5 周把第一、第二沉思放在一起对照。每节一小步一小步走：背景 → 论证 → 例子和思想实验 → 反驳与回应 → 易错点 → 小测验。标着「High-yield」的小节，是本站认为测验可能会问到的重点；标着「必会 Must know」的，是后面内容的基础。这两个标签都是本站自己的判断，不是老师公布的范围，也不表示哪个内容考得多。读懂一节就点「我学会了 Mark as learned」；每周最后的「考点清单 Exam focus」列出本站认为这一周可能会怎么考。
howToUse.en: Read week by week in Learn. Week 2 has 13 sections and every other week 14; each section teaches one reading, its title starts with the author (for example 'Russell: ...') or, for Plato's dialogues, with the dialogue ('Apology: ...', 'Meno: ...'), and it shows Reading page numbers, the pages of the PDF on Quercus, so you can check the original; Plato's dialogues also give the section numbers printed in the margin (such as 21d). The last section of Weeks 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 is a comparison whose title starts with 'Comparison:' and which has no page numbers of its own: it compares the week's two readings in Weeks 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9, the two halves of the Meno in Week 4, and the First and Second Meditations in Week 5. Each section goes in small steps: context, the argument, examples and thought experiments, objections and replies, common traps and a quick check. The High-yield badge marks what this site thinks a test may well ask about, and Must know marks the basics later sections build on; both badges are this site's own judgement, not an official scope, and they say nothing about how often anything is tested. When a section makes sense, press Mark as learned. The Exam focus list at the end of each week gives this site's view of how the week could be tested.

howToUse.zh: 「考试这样写 Exam English」方框里是能直接写上考卷的英文：一句话的论点、标准形式的论证、定义、反驳和回应。写的时候把作者的观点和你自己的评价分开：先写“Russell argues that ...”“According to Hume, ...”，再写“One objection is that ...”“I think this premise is weak because ...”。术语按读物的写法：罗素的 sense-data，休谟的 sceptical，范·因瓦根大写的 Realism 和 anti-Realism（和小写的 realism 不是一回事）；Grube 译本的 piety、the pious 和 true opinion，Cottingham 译本的 malicious demon 和 I am, I exist（第 5 周的读物里没有 I think, therefore I am 这句话，那是罗素在第 7 周转述笛卡尔时用的）。本站只引用很短的关键原话，其余都是用自己的话改写的；你答题时也一样，用自己的英文把作者的意思说准确。
howToUse.en: The Exam English boxes hold English you can write on the test: a one-sentence thesis, an argument in standard form, a definition, an objection and a reply. Keep the author's view apart from your own assessment: first 'Russell argues that ...' or 'According to Hume, ...', then 'One objection is that ...' or 'I think this premise is weak because ...'. Use each reading's own terms and spelling: Russell's sense-data, Hume's 'sceptical', van Inwagen's capital-R Realism and anti-Realism (not the same thing as lowercase realism), Grube's 'piety', 'the pious' and 'true opinion', and Cottingham's 'malicious demon' and 'I am, I exist' ('I think, therefore I am' is not in the Week 5 reading; it is how Russell reports Descartes in Week 7). The site quotes only very short key phrases and puts everything else in its own words; do the same in your answers and state the author's point accurately in your own English.

howToUse.zh: 标着「补充 Extra」、开头写着“补充（读物外）”的提示框，讲的是读物以外的背景，比如后人起的名字“休谟之叉”（Hume's fork）和“自然齐一性”（uniformity of nature）。补充（读物外）：第 3–5 周常见的“游叙弗伦困境”（Euthyphro dilemma）、“美诺悖论”（Meno's paradox）、cogito（我思）和 evil demon 也都是后人起的名字，译本里没有。考试以读物和讲课为准。本站只有读物：没有讲课课件，没有辅导课材料（第 6 周辅导课继续讨论笛卡尔，本站也没有），也没有辛顿（**Geoffrey Hinton**）的视频讲座《Will AI Outsmart Human Intelligence?》；第 10 周查默斯那一讲在大纲里也是视频讲座，本站用的是他的书面论文。测验和期末都考全部课程内容，讲课补充的东西要靠你自己的笔记。讲课和读物说法不一样时，写清楚你用的是哪一个（“In the lecture, ...”“In the reading, ...”）。
howToUse.en: Notes labelled Extra give background beyond the readings, such as later labels like 'Hume's fork' and 'the uniformity of nature'. Extra (not in the readings): the familiar names 'Euthyphro dilemma', 'Meno's paradox', 'cogito' and 'evil demon' for Weeks 3-5 are later labels too, which the translations do not use. For the tests, the readings and the lectures come first. The station has the readings only: no lecture slides, no tutorial material (the Week 6 tutorials continued Descartes, and the station has nothing from them either), and nothing from Geoffrey Hinton's video lecture 'Will AI Outsmart Human Intelligence?'; the Week 10 Chalmers session is also a video lecture in the syllabus, and the station uses his written paper. The tests and the final exam cover all course content, so for what the lectures add, use your own notes. When the lecture's wording differs from the reading's, say which one you are using ('In the lecture, ...', 'In the reading, ...').

howToUse.zh: 每个例子和思想实验（**thought experiment**）都在「例题 Worked example」方框里一步一步走完，最后会写出“它想说明什么”：哈特引用的泰勒森林圆球，苏格拉底的神谕和牛虻，《美诺篇》的奴隶男孩、去拉里萨的路和代达罗斯的雕像，笛卡尔的炉火边、恶魔和蜡块，罗素的桌子和猫，休谟的亚当和台球，古德曼的祖母绿和 grue，内格尔的蝙蝠，查默斯的逐步上传和《人生切割术》（Severance）。测验和期末都可能问“这个例子说明了什么”，所以每个例子都要能用一句英文回答。反驳与回应多半放在「讨论题 Discuss」里：先自己用英文想一个回答，再点「看参考答案」。讲义里还有分类练习（比如第 2 周：这是因果的问题，还是存在论的问题？第 8 周：这句话是观念的关系，还是实际的事情？），练到不用想就能分对。
howToUse.en: Every example and **thought experiment** is walked through step by step in a Worked example box that ends with what it is meant to show: Taylor's sphere in Hart, Socrates' oracle and gadfly, the slave boy, the road to Larissa and the statues of Daedalus in the Meno, Descartes' fireside, malicious demon and wax, Russell's table and cat, Hume's Adam and billiard balls, Goodman's emeralds and grue, Nagel's bat, Chalmers's gradual uploading and Severance. A test or the final may ask what an example shows, so be able to answer in one English sentence for each. Objections and replies are mostly in Discuss boxes: think of your own English answer first, then press Show model answer. The lessons also have sorting drills (for example in Week 2: is this question aetiological or ontological? In Week 8: is this statement a relation of ideas or a matter of fact?); practise until you sort them without thinking.

howToUse.zh: 学完一周，点每周最后的「练习这一课」，或者去「刷题 Practice」。题目和真实测验一样用英文出，三种题型都有：选择题（本站每题 4 个选项，大纲没说真实测验每题几个选项）、判断题和多选题，还有简答题和小论文；看不懂就点「显示中文」。每周大约 45–60 道题。先在「题型筛选」里点「只做客观题 Objective only」，练选择和判断；再点「只做主观题 Written only」练写作：先用英文写下答案，再点「对照参考答案自评」，勾出写到的得分点（写到一半就算对）。小论文的参考答案大约 140–180 个英文单词：论点、作者的论证、一个反驳、回应或评价。
howToUse.en: After each week, press Practice this lesson at the end of it, or go to Practice. Questions are in English like the real test, and all three types are there: multiple choice (4 options each here; the syllabus does not say how many options the real test has), true/false and select-all, plus short answers and short essays; tap Show Chinese when you are stuck. Each week has about 45-60 questions. First press Objective only under Question types for the multiple-choice and true/false questions, then Written only for the writing: write your English answer first, then press Compare and grade yourself and tick the scoring points you covered (half of them counts as correct). Short-essay model answers are about 140-180 English words: the thesis, the author's argument, one objection, and a reply or assessment.

howToUse.zh: 测验只用英文，术语一定要认得、会写。「术语表」里每周大约 25–40 个术语，有英文定义和中文解释；用「闪卡」来背：先练「英→中」（看到英文认得意思），再练「中→英」（自己想出英文），熟了以后勾选「只练不熟的卡」。特别要分清长得像、意思却不同的一对对词：wonder 和 curiosity，ontological 和 aetiological，instinctive person（第 2 周）和 instinctive belief（第 7 周），the pious 和 the god-loved，knowledge 和 true opinion，malicious demon 和 deceiving God，sense-data 和 physical object，realism 和 Realism，relations of ideas 和 matters of fact，lawlike 和 accidental，green 和 grue，subjective 和 objective，physicalism 和 functionalism，quasi-belief 和 belief。
howToUse.en: The tests use English only, so you must recognize and write every term. The Glossary has about 25-40 terms per week with English definitions and Chinese explanations; drill them with Flashcards: first EN to ZH (recognize the meaning), then ZH to EN (recall the English), then tick Only unfamiliar cards. Take special care with pairs that look alike but mean different things: wonder and curiosity, ontological and aetiological, the instinctive person (Week 2) and instinctive beliefs (Week 7), the pious and the god-loved, knowledge and true opinion, the malicious demon and the deceiving God, sense-data and physical objects, realism and Realism, relations of ideas and matters of fact, lawlike and accidental, green and grue, subjective and objective, physicalism and functionalism, quasi-belief and belief.

howToUse.zh: 答错的题会自动进「错题本」，之后答对了就自动移出。每天花 10 分钟清一清：按周点「重练本单元」，或者点「全部重练」。每道错题都问自己：是论证没记住，是两个作者或两个术语搞混了（比如把休谟的问题当成古德曼的），还是英文题目没读懂？
howToUse.en: Wrong answers go to the mistake book automatically and leave once you answer them correctly. Spend 10 minutes a day clearing it, week by week with Retry unit or all at once with Retry all. For each wrong answer, ask: did I forget the argument, mix up two authors or two terms (Hume's problem with Goodman's, say), or misread the English?

howToUse.zh: 用「模拟考」检验自己：默认设置是本站八周全选、15 道客观题（选择、判断、多选）加 3 道主观题（简答或小论文）、50 分钟。为测验 2 练习时，先点「清空 None」，再只勾第 7–10 周；为期末练习时保留八周全选，可以把题量和时间调大（本站没有第 11–13 周的题）。大纲没写真实测验或期末各有几道，这只是练习用的估计，真实题量看 Quercus 公告。像真考一样限时作答，不点“显示中文”。交卷后客观题自动判分，主观题对照参考答案自评；成绩单按周告诉你哪里最弱。题目和「刷题」来自同一个题库，所以每道题都要重新想，不要凭记忆选。
howToUse.en: Test yourself with the Mock exam. Its default settings are all eight weeks of the station, 15 objective questions (multiple choice, true/false, select-all) plus 3 written ones (short answer or short essay), 50 minutes. To practise for Test 2, press None and then tick only Weeks 7-10; for the final, keep all eight weeks and raise the numbers and the time (the station has no questions on Weeks 11-13). The syllabus does not say how many questions of each type the real test or the final has, so this is only a practice estimate; the Quercus announcements have the real numbers. Work under the time limit without Show Chinese. Objective questions are graded when you hand in, you grade the written ones against the model answers, and the report shows your weakest week. The questions come from the same banks as Practice, so think every question through again instead of answering from memory.

howToUse.zh: 考前用「速记」（考前速记）：每篇读物只留 3–4 条重点（问什么、答什么、怎么论证、别搞错什么），每周再加几个必会术语，可以打印。时间不够就先看每篇的第一条。「答题」里的英文答题工具箱教你用英文写答案：指令词（explain、reconstruct、evaluate、compare……）、答题模板（把论证写成标准形式、解释思想实验、提出反驳并给出作者的回应、比较两篇读物、写小论文……）、常用句型、常见英文错误，以及 50 分钟测验和 3 小时期末的答题策略。
howToUse.en: Before a test, use the Cheat sheet: only 3-4 key points for each reading (the question, the answer, the main argument and the one thing not to confuse), plus a few must-know terms for each week; you can print it. If time is short, read each reading's first point first. The Exam English toolkit teaches you to write answers in English: question verbs (explain, reconstruct, evaluate, compare...), answer templates (put an argument in standard form, explain a thought experiment, raise an objection and give the author's reply, compare two readings, write a short essay...), useful phrases, common English mistakes, and strategies for the 50-minute test and the 3-hour final.

howToUse.zh: 跟着「学习计划」走（测验 2 冲刺计划和期末复习计划），做完一项打一个勾。进度只保存在这台设备的浏览器里，换电脑或清理浏览器之前，先到「设置」导出备份。「设置」里还能换语言模式：刚开始用「中文优先」，平时用「中英平衡」，考前换成「英文练习」（中文先模糊，逼自己先读英文）。考试时间、考场、题量这些官方信息，永远以老师在 Quercus 上公布的为准。本站只用来复习，不能用来完成测验或辅导课练习。
howToUse.en: Follow a Study plan (the Test 2 sprint plan or the final exam plan) and tick each task when it is done. intro.zh:
这门课的副标题是“知识与实在”。本站的八周，其实在追问同一串问题：哲学是什么，值得做吗？我们看到的，是不是世界真实的样子？什么才算真正知道，有没有什么东西经得起一切怀疑？我们凭什么相信还没看到的东西？我们自己的意识又是什么，机器能不能有？
第 2 周（哲学）：哈特说，哲学从惊奇（**wonder**）开始：不是好奇缺了哪个事实，而是惊讶竟然有东西存在；一个东西“是什么”解释不了它“存在着”，所以这个谜是存在论的（**ontological**），不只是因果的（**aetiological**）。罗素说，哲学通常给不出确定的答案，它的价值很大程度上就在这种不确定：它让思想摆脱习俗的暴政（**tyranny of custom**），去掉傲慢的独断，并通过沉思宇宙的伟大，让心灵也变得广大。
第 3 周（哲学）：德尔斐神谕说没有人比苏格拉底更智慧；他盘问了政治家、诗人和工匠，发现自己只在一点上更智慧：他不以为自己知道自己不知道的事（人的智慧，**human wisdom**）。在《申辩篇》里，他宁可服从神、继续审视别人，也不肯为了活命而停下；在《游叙弗伦篇》里，他请游叙弗伦说出让一切虔敬的行为都虔敬的那一个型（形式，**form**），游叙弗伦的定义一个个失败，最后绕回原点。
第 4 周（知识）：《美诺篇》问美德（**virtue**）能不能教，苏格拉底说要先知道美德是什么。面对“探究不可能”的论证，他提出学习就是回忆（**recollection**），并让一个奴隶男孩做几何题来演示；最后他区分知识和真意见（**true opinion**）：真意见带路不比知识差，但要用对原因的说明拴住，才成为知识。
第 5 周（知识）：笛卡尔用一层比一层强的理由（感官、做梦、骗人的上帝），把一切不完全确定的信念先放一边，又有意假设一个恶意的恶魔；然后找到一个固定的点：每当他说出或想到“我在，我存在”，它就一定为真。他是一个思维之物（**a thing that thinks**），而且蜡块说明，心灵比物体更容易被认识。
第 7 周（实在）：罗素说，桌子的颜色、质地、形状都随观察者和条件而变，我们直接知道的只是感觉材料（**sense-data**），真实的桌子要靠推论；外部世界没法严格证明，但它是更简单的假设，也是一种本能信念。范·因瓦根论证有客观真理（**objective truth**）：信念的真假由世界决定，不由信念本身决定。
第 8 周（知识）：休谟说，从“过去一直如此”推到“将来也会如此”，没有任何推理能支持，是习惯（**custom**）在带我们走。古德曼的 grue 提出另一个问题：同样的证据，到底确证哪一个假说？
第 9 周（心灵）：内格尔说，有意识就是“成为这个生物是有某种样子的”（对它自己来说），物理描述抓不住这种主观特征（蝙蝠）。查默斯论证，把大脑一块块换成功能相同的元件，意识会一直保持。
第 10 周（人工智能）：查默斯问，和大语言模型（**LLM**）聊天时，对话者到底是什么。他的回答：不是模型本身，也不是某台服务器，而是虚拟实例或线程。
一张桌子就能把第 7–10 周串起来。罗素问：你看到的棕色，是桌子本身的颜色吗？用休谟的问题来问：你凭什么相信这张桌子明天还托得住你的书？用内格尔和查默斯的问题来问：“看到棕色”是什么样子？知道你大脑的全部物理事实，能不能告诉你这一点？再用查默斯在第 10 周的说法：如果一个聊天机器人的行为可以被解释为相信“桌子是棕色的”，而且这样解释能让它的行为说得通、帮我们预测它会怎么做，它就有这个准信念（**quasi-belief**），但这不等于它真的相信，更不等于它有意识。第 2–5 周也接得上：哈特会问的不是桌子由什么构成、怎么来的，而是它为什么竟然存在；笛卡尔会先问：你怎么知道自己不是在做梦？他自己就以为坐在炉火边，又想起常常梦见同样的场景。
每篇读物都靠论证说话，所以四条主线下面还有一条贯穿八周的线：怎样读论证、评论证。
intro.en:
The course's subtitle is Knowledge and Reality. The station's eight weeks keep asking one chain of questions: what is philosophy, and is it worth doing? Is what we see the way the world really is? What counts as really knowing, and can anything survive every doubt? Why do we believe things we have not yet seen? And what is our own consciousness, and could a machine have it?
Week 2 (philosophy): Hart says that philosophy begins in **wonder**: not curiosity about a missing fact, but surprise that anything exists at all; what a thing is cannot explain that it is, so the mystery is **ontological**, not merely **aetiological**. Russell says that philosophy usually cannot give definite answers and that its value lies largely in this uncertainty: it frees our thinking from the **tyranny of custom**, removes arrogant dogmatism and, by contemplating the greatness of the universe, makes the mind great too.
Week 3 (philosophy): the oracle at Delphi said that no one was wiser than Socrates; after questioning politicians, poets and craftsmen, he found that he was wiser in one way only: he does not think he knows what he does not know (**human wisdom**). In the Apology he would rather obey the god and keep examining people than stop to save his life; in the Euthyphro he asks Euthyphro for the one **form** that makes all pious actions pious, and every definition Euthyphro offers fails until the argument comes back to where it started.
Week 4 (knowledge): the Meno asks whether **virtue** can be taught, and Socrates says we must first know what virtue is. Against the argument that inquiry is impossible, he proposes that learning is **recollection** and demonstrates it with a slave boy and a geometry problem; at the end he separates knowledge from **true opinion**: true opinion guides as well as knowledge, but it becomes knowledge only when it is tied down by an account of the reason why.
Week 5 (knowledge): Descartes sets aside every belief that is not completely certain, with stronger and stronger reasons for doubt (the senses, dreaming, a deceiving God), and deliberately supposes a malicious demon; then he finds one firm point: 'I am, I exist' must be true whenever he asserts it or thinks it. He is **a thing that thinks**, and the wax shows that the mind is known better than the body.
Week 7 (reality): Russell argues that the table's colour, texture and shape all vary with the observer and the conditions, so what we know directly are **sense-data**, and the real table has to be inferred; the external world cannot be strictly proved, but it is the simpler hypothesis and an instinctive belief. Van Inwagen argues that there is **objective truth**: the World, not our believing, makes our beliefs true or false.
Week 8 (knowledge): Hume argues that no reasoning takes us from 'it has always been so' to 'it will be so'; **custom** carries us there. Goodman's grue raises a different question: which hypothesis does a body of evidence confirm?
Week 9 (mind): Nagel says that a creature is conscious when there is something it is like to be the creature, for the creature itself, and physical descriptions miss this subjective character (the bat). Chalmers argues that if a brain were replaced piece by piece with functionally identical parts, consciousness would stay.
Week 10 (artificial intelligence): Chalmers asks what the interlocutor is when we chat with a large language model (**LLM**). His answer: not the model itself and not any one server, but a virtual instance or a thread.
One table connects Weeks 7-10. Russell asks: is the brown you see the table's own colour? Ask Hume's question: why do you believe the table will still hold your books tomorrow? Ask Nagel's and Chalmers's question: what is it like to see brown, and would knowing every physical fact about your brain tell you? And in Chalmers's Week 10 terms: if a chatbot's behaviour can be interpreted as believing that the table is brown, in a way that makes sense of what it does and helps predict it, it has that **quasi-belief**, which does not mean that it really believes it, let alone that it is conscious. Weeks 2-5 join in too: Hart would ask not what the table is made of or where it came from, but why it exists at all; and Descartes would first ask how you know you are not dreaming: he believed he was sitting by the fire, then remembered how often he had dreamt just such scenes.
Every reading makes its case through arguments, so under the four branches runs one thread through all eight weeks: how to read and assess an argument.

title.zh: 哲学是什么：惊奇与追问
title.en: What philosophy is: wonder and questioning

summary.zh:
第 2、3 周问：哲学从哪里来，值不值得做，又该怎么做？
第 2 周，哈特（**Hart**）的 'Being'（第三章 'Being (Sat)' 的节选）：他沿着柏拉图和亚里士多德的说法，认为哲学开始于惊奇（**wonder**）。惊奇不是好奇（缺一个事实，查到就解决），而是突然意识到：任何事实都解释不了竟然有东西存在这个谜。小孩子也许更能感到世界的被给予，大人却让习惯取代了敬畏。在那一瞬间我们看到，一个东西“是什么”（本质，**essence**）解释不了它“存在着”（存在，**existence**），没有东西能让自己存在，所以世界是绝对偶然的（**absolute contingency**）：本来可以是别的样子，也本来可以根本不存在，用哈特的话说：“It need not be at all.”（第 4 页）。有人把这种惊讶说成像似曾相识那样的大脑故障，或者说存在的问题只是语法造成的混乱、根本说不通；哈特回应：这是在推卸思考的责任。核心论证：物理的、因果的解释只能用一个偶然之物去解释另一个，一路追到最小的粒子或最初的奇点，到达的仍是偶然之物，所以这个谜是存在论的（**ontological**），不只是因果的（**aetiological**）。泰勒（**Richard Taylor**）的森林圆球：在森林里碰到一个半透明的大圆球，我们会问它为什么在那儿；同样的问题也可以问一块石头、一棵树，圆球像宇宙那么大、一直存在也一样，只是因为熟悉，我们才不问。存在上的贫乏（**ontological poverty**）：每个有限的东西都依赖自身以外的东西。最后他说，认真思考偶然性一定会碰到上帝的问题，但他没有证明上帝存在。
罗素（**Bertrand Russell**）的 'The Value of Philosophy'：哲学不像科学那样对不学它的人有用，它的价值是间接的（**indirect value**），在心灵的好处之中。哲学看起来没有确定的答案，部分是因为一旦能确定回答，那门学问就独立成了科学（天文学、心理学），剩下的才叫哲学（本站把这叫“剩余物”论证）；有些问题也许永远无解，哲学仍要让它们保持活力。哲学的价值很大程度上就在它的不确定：没有哲学的人被关在常识、时代和国家的习惯信念、理性没检查过的看法里；哲学减少我们对“事物是什么”的确定感，却大大增加我们对“事物可能是什么”的知识，让思想摆脱习俗的暴政（**tyranny of custom**），去掉傲慢的独断（**arrogant dogmatism**），保持惊奇。另一种价值是沉思宇宙的伟大：它扩大自我（**Self**），让我们摆脱狭隘的私人目标，成为宇宙公民（**citizens of the universe**）。所以学哲学是为了问题本身，不是为了确定的答案。
第 3 周，柏拉图（**Plato**）笔下的苏格拉底（**Socrates**），译者是 **G.M.A. Grube**。《申辩篇》（**Apology**）是苏格拉底在法庭上的辩护词（apologia 是辩护，不是道歉）。他先回应早先的控告者（流言说他研究天上地下的事、把较弱的论证说成较强的、收费授课），再回应美勒托（**Meletus**）、安尼图斯（**Anytus**）和吕孔（**Lycon**）的正式指控：败坏青年，不信城邦的神而信新的精灵之事。德尔斐神谕说没有人比他更智慧；他盘问了政治家、诗人和工匠，得出：他只在一点上更智慧，就是不以为自己知道自己不知道的事（21d）。这就是人的智慧（**human wisdom**）；注意，他从没说过“我只知道我一无所知”。他论证怕死是一种假智慧，因为谁也不知道死是好是坏；他宁可服从神，也不服从陪审团（“I will obey the god rather than you”，第 8 页，29d）；他把自己比作神派给雅典的牛虻（**gadfly**）；他的神圣征兆（**divine sign**）只会阻止他做事，让他远离政治。被判有罪以后，他说“the unexamined life is not worth living”（第 12 页，38a）。判了死刑，他又说死要么像无梦的睡眠，要么是灵魂迁到另一个地方，两种都不是坏事；他说的是有好的希望，不是知道。
《游叙弗伦篇》（**Euthyphro**）：游叙弗伦自称精确知道什么是虔敬（**piety**），正要告自己的父亲。苏格拉底要的是让一切虔敬的行为都虔敬的那一个型（形式，**form**），举一个例子不算定义。“神所喜爱的就是虔敬的”失败，因为诸神意见不合，同一件事就会既虔敬又不虔敬。接着是那个两难（补充（读物外）：后人叫它“游叙弗伦困境”，**Euthyphro dilemma**）：诸神爱虔敬的东西，是因为它虔敬，还是它因为被神爱才虔敬？游叙弗伦选前一支，所以被神爱只是虔敬的“an affect or a quality”（第 8 页，11a），不是虔敬本身。后面的定义（照料神、服侍神、懂得献祭和祈祷，等于神与人之间的一种交易）也都失败，最后绕回“神所喜爱的”，没有答案就结束了。
一句话分清（本站的理解）：第 2 周讲哲学为什么值得做（惊奇，不确定的价值）；第 3 周让你看到苏格拉底怎样做哲学：承认自己不知道，再追问“X 是什么”。
summary.en:
Weeks 2 and 3 ask where philosophy comes from, whether it is worth doing, and how to do it.
Week 2, Hart's 'Being' (a selection from Chapter Three, 'Being (Sat)'): following Plato and Aristotle, Hart holds that philosophy begins in **wonder**. Wonder is not curiosity (a missing fact that we can look up); it is the sudden awareness that no fact could explain the mystery that anything exists at all. Small children may sense the world's givenness more openly, but adults let habit replace awe. In that moment we see that what a thing is (its **essence**) does not explain that it is (its **existence**) and that nothing can give itself existence, so the world is absolutely contingent (**absolute contingency**): it could have been different, and in Hart's words, "It need not be at all" (p. 4). People explain this surprise away as a brain glitch like déjà vu, or dismiss the question of existence as a muddle of grammar or as meaningless; Hart replies that this gives up the responsibility to think. His core argument: physical, causal explanations only explain one contingent thing by another, and following the chain down to the smallest particles or back to the first singularity still ends with contingent things, so the mystery is **ontological**, not merely **aetiological**. Richard Taylor's sphere: a walker who found a large translucent sphere in a forest would ask why it is there; the same question can be asked about a rock or a tree, or about a sphere as big as the universe that has always existed, and only familiarity stops us from asking it. **Ontological poverty**: every finite thing depends on things outside itself. Finally, Hart says that serious thought about contingency must raise the question of God, but he does not prove that God exists.
Russell's 'The Value of Philosophy': unlike science, philosophy is not useful to people who never study it; its value is indirect (**indirect value**) and lies among the goods of the mind. Philosophy seems to have no definite answers partly because a subject becomes a separate science (astronomy, psychology) as soon as definite answers are possible, and what is left is called philosophy (the station calls this the residue argument); some questions may never be answered, but philosophy must keep them alive. Its value lies largely in its uncertainty: a person without philosophy is imprisoned in common sense, in the beliefs of his age or nation and in convictions his reason never examined; philosophy lowers our certainty about what things are but greatly increases our knowledge of what they may be, frees our thinking from the **tyranny of custom**, removes **arrogant dogmatism** and keeps wonder alive. A second value is the contemplation of the greatness of the universe: it enlarges the **Self**, frees us from narrow private aims and makes us **citizens of the universe**. So philosophy should be studied for the sake of its questions, not for definite answers.
Week 3, Plato's Socrates, translated by G.M.A. Grube. The **Apology** is Socrates' defence speech at his trial (apologia means a defence, not saying sorry). He first answers the old accusers, whose rumours said that he studied the heavens and what lies under the earth, made the worse argument the stronger and taught for fees, and then the formal charge brought by Meletus, Anytus and Lycon: corrupting the young and not believing in the city's gods but in new spiritual things. The oracle at Delphi said that no one was wiser than Socrates; after questioning politicians, poets and craftsmen, he concluded that he was wiser in one way only: he does not think he knows what he does not know (21d). This is **human wisdom**; note that he never says 'I know that I know nothing'. He argues that fearing death is false wisdom, since no one knows whether death is good or bad; he would obey the god rather than the jury ("I will obey the god rather than you", p. 8, 29d); he compares himself to a **gadfly** attached to Athens by the god; and his **divine sign** only ever turns him away from things, and it kept him out of politics. After the guilty verdict he declares, "the unexamined life is not worth living" (p. 12, 38a). Once sentenced to death, he argues that death is either like a dreamless sleep or a move of the soul to another place, and neither is bad; he claims good hope, not knowledge.
The **Euthyphro**: Euthyphro claims to know precisely what **piety** is and is prosecuting his own father. Socrates asks for the one **form** that makes all pious actions pious; an example is not a definition. 'The pious is what is dear to the gods' fails because the gods disagree, so one and the same act would be both pious and impious. Then comes the dilemma (Extra (not in the reading): later writers call it the Euthyphro dilemma): do the gods love the pious for being pious, or does their love make it pious? Euthyphro takes the first horn, so being loved by the gods is only "an affect or a quality" of the pious (p. 8, 11a), not what the pious is. The later definitions (care of the gods, service to the gods, and knowing how to sacrifice and pray, which makes piety a kind of trade between gods and men) also fail, and the argument comes back to 'dear to the gods'; the dialogue ends without an answer.
In one line (this station's interpretation): Week 2 asks why philosophy is worth doing (wonder and the value of uncertainty); Week 3 shows how Socrates does it: he admits what he does not know and keeps asking 'What is X?'.

summary.zh:
第 7 周两篇读物。罗素（**Bertrand Russell**）《The Problems of Philosophy》第 1–2 章问：有没有任何讲道理的人都无法怀疑的知识？第 1 章拿一张桌子来想：颜色随视角、灯光、色盲、蓝色眼镜而变，在黑暗里根本没有颜色；显微镜下的质地和肉眼看到的不同；形状随角度而变，“真实的形状”是推出来的，不是看到的；手感随按压的力度而变。所以我们直接知道的只是感觉材料（**sense-data**：颜色、声音、软硬等；觉察到它们叫感觉 **sensation**），真实的桌子（物理对象 **physical object**）如果存在，只能推论出来。由此两个问题：有没有物质（**matter**）？如果有，它是什么样的？唯心论（**idealism**）者贝克莱（**George Berkeley**）说，真实的桌子是上帝心中的观念，莱布尼茨（**Leibniz**）说它是一群灵魂；罗素认为唯心论的一般论证是谬误。第 2 章：笛卡尔（**René Descartes**）的系统怀疑和“我思故我在”；罗素修正说，确定的只是“一个棕色正被看到”，而不是一个持久的“我”。“整个人生是一场梦”在逻辑上无法反驳；但相信独立的物体更简单（猫在没人看时也会饿；人说话是在表达思想），这又是一种本能信念（**instinctive belief**），所以可以接受，只保留一点来自梦的怀疑。哲学的任务：把本能信念排成和谐的体系。
范·因瓦根（**Peter van Inwagen**）《Objectivity》问：有没有客观真理？客观真理有两部分：信念描绘世界，要么真要么假（像地图要对得上地形）；世界在很大程度上不依赖我们的信念。真理只有一个，“对我来说是真的”其实只是“我是这么想的”；相信客观真理也不等于独断：其他星球上有没有智慧生命，现在谁也不知道，但要么有，要么没有。他分清两组词：小写的 realism 对唯心论（是不是一切都是心灵的？），大写的 **Realism** 对 **anti-Realism**（有没有客观真理？），所以唯心论者也可以是大写的 Realist。地质论证：珠穆朗玛峰高 8,849 米；地质学解释这个高度时完全用不到心灵，所以在一个从来没有心灵的世界里，它也一样高。“社会建构”论证只说明约定决定了“Mount Everest”这个名字指哪块岩石、“高度”这个词指哪种性质（schmeight 的例子），决定不了事物本身有多高。最后，反实在论看来是自我反驳的（**self-refuting**）：代替“真”的地位必须既属于所有公认的好陈述，又属于反实在论自己，而反实在论者提出过的每一种替代品，反实在论本身似乎都不具备。结论：我们应该做 Realist。
第 7 周最后一节讲一个关键区分：两种“实在论”之争。罗素问的是实在论对唯心论，范·因瓦根问的是 Realism 对 anti-Realism。
summary.en:
Week 7 has two readings. Russell's The Problems of Philosophy, Chapters 1-2, asks whether any knowledge is so certain that no reasonable person could doubt it. Chapter 1 thinks about a table: its colour changes with the point of view, the lighting, a colour-blind viewer or blue spectacles, and in the dark it has no colour at all; its texture under a microscope differs from what the naked eye sees; its shape changes with the angle, so its 'real' shape is inferred, not seen; and how hard it feels depends on how hard we press. So what we know directly are **sense-data** (colours, sounds, hardnesses and so on; being aware of them is **sensation**), and the real table, the **physical object**, if there is one, can only be inferred. Hence two questions: is there any **matter**, and if so, what is it like? The idealist Berkeley says the real table is an idea in the mind of God, Leibniz says it is a colony of souls, and Russell judges the general argument for **idealism** fallacious. Chapter 2: Descartes' method of systematic doubt and 'I think, therefore I am'; Russell corrects it: what is certain is that 'a brown colour is being seen', not that a lasting 'I' sees it. That life is one long dream cannot be logically refuted, but believing in independent objects is simpler (a cat gets hungry even when no one is looking; people's speech expresses thought), and it is an **instinctive belief**, so we may accept it, keeping only a slight doubt that comes from dreams. Philosophy's job is to arrange our instinctive beliefs into a harmonious system.
Van Inwagen's 'Objectivity' asks whether there is objective truth. It has two parts: beliefs represent the World and are true or false (as a map must fit the territory), and the World is in large part independent of our beliefs. Truth is one, and 'true for me' only means 'what I think'; believing in objective truth is not dogmatism: no one now knows whether other planets have intelligent life, but either they do or they do not. He separates two pairs of words: lowercase realism vs idealism (is everything mental?) and capital-R **Realism** vs **anti-Realism** (is there objective truth?), so an idealist can be a Realist. The geological argument: Mount Everest is 8,849 meters high, and since geology explains that height without any help from minds, it would be just as high in a world without minds. The 'social construct' argument only shows that conventions fix which rock the name 'Mount Everest' picks out and which property the word 'height' names (the schmeight example), not how high things are. Finally, anti-Realism seems to be **self-refuting**: a substitute for truth would have to belong both to all clearly good statements and to anti-Realism itself, and every substitute anti-Realists have offered seems to be one that anti-Realism itself lacks. Conclusion: we should be Realists.
A key distinction comes in the last section of Week 7: the two debates about 'realism'. Russell's question is realism vs idealism; van Inwagen's is Realism vs anti-Realism.
